title: Sandbox: a dev bench that builds agent-usage scenarios into .sandbox/
body: An exploratory workspace, not a test. It builds a state and leaves it for inspection; anything learned there becomes a formal test in tests/cli.rs against a throwaway repo, and the bench never grows assertions. Form: examples/sandbox.rs, run with cargo run --example sandbox <scenario>, driving the built foam binary through std::process. .sandbox/ at the project root is git-ignored, one subdirectory per scenario, rebuilt from scratch each run, with a bare origin.git on disk and one clone per simulated agent so sync, the pre-push hook and merges run without a network. The repo, clone and actor helpers move to a module shared with tests/cli.rs so a scenario line and a test line look alike. A scenario is a function of a few lines: actors, calls, done. Each records the prime text every simulated session would have seen. First scenarios: one session (prime, claim, note, close, remember); two agents on two clones claiming the same issue and both pushing; a dead agent (lease-minutes 0, next prime reclaims); an agent that files an epic and children mid-task; a big backlog (200 issues, 30 memories) for prime size and search.
